To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) domain adaptation in deep models can be achieved by backpropagation and (ii) the adaptation behaviour can be promoted by a gradient reversal layer that is added to the model

(1) we propose a new domain adaptation method for deep neural networks that is based on the idea of minimizing the difference between source and target domain distributions, (2) the method is based on a novel gradient reversal layer that reverses the gradients during the backpropagation phase, and (3) the proposed method is very easy to implement and achieves state of the art results on Office datasets

(i) deep architectures can be trained to learn features invariant to domain shifts by backpropagation; (ii) the approach is simple to implement in any feedforward deep architecture and can be trained using any of the standard deep learning packages; (iii) it can be used in the absence of any labeled target data; (iv) it performs better than previous state of the arts on Office datasets.

domain adaptation can be achieved in a simple and effective way by using a single augmented deep model that can be trained by backpropagation.
domain adaptation in deep networks can be achieved with little effort and no additional learning algorithm.
